name: Islamo-leftism
summary: Islamo-leftism (French 'islamo-gauchisme') is a label, coined or popularised by Pierre-André Taguieff in 2002, for a supposed alliance between left-wing currents and Islamism, said by its users to rest on shared anti-Zionism, anti-imperialism and opposition to globalisation. The scholarship describes it as a polemical term with no adherents, programme or normative worldview of its own.

notFound.work: A programme, manifesto or self-description by any group calling itself Islamo-leftist

tried.how: read Marlière 2023, Berkley Center response, The World report for tenets

scope: The name as the defining sources use it: a French polemical label (Taguieff 2002, Vidal 2021) for alleged left-Islamist convergence. Marlière states that it cannot be described as an ideology. Islamic socialism, the Iranian Islamic left and the left movements it targets are other subjects and answer nothing here.
